A '''circle''' is a set of all points of equal distance from a given point in a given [[plane]].

An '''arc''' is part of a circle.

== Formal definition ==

Let $\mathcal{X}=(\mathbb{F}^2,d)$ be a [[metric space|2-dimensional metric space]].

Set of points

$$
\{P:d(P,O)=r,\, r \in \mathbb{R}^+\}
$$

is called the '''circle''' of radius $r$ centered at $O$ in $\mathcal{X}$,denoted by $\bigcirc O_r$.

[[File:Circle-O-r-P1-20.svg|thumbnail|A circle in the [[Euclidean circle|Euclidean plane]]. In reality, there are an infinite number of points $P$s. There is no way to draw all of them at once.]]

Any of its subsets, $A \subseteq \bigcirc O_r$, is an '''arc''' of radius $r$ centered at $O$.

== Terminologies ==

=== Lines, segments, and arcs ===

* '''Radius''': A segment from the centre to any point on the circle.

<blockquote>
Confusingly, the length of a radius is also called radius.
</blockquote>

* '''Diameter''': Segment formed by extending a radius beyond the centre of the circle until another intersection with the circle.
* '''Circumference''': The perimeter around the circle.
* '''Chord''': A segment whose endpoints lie on the circle.
* '''Secant''': A line that intersects the circle at two points.
* '''Tangent''': A line that intersects the circle at exactly one point.
* '''Point of tangency''': The point where a tangent touches the circle.
** '''Minor arc''': Shorter arc between two points on the circle.
** '''Major arc''': Longer arc between two points on the circle.
** '''Semicircle''': Arc equal to half the circle.

=== Angles ===

* '''Central angle''': An angle whose vertex is the centre of the circle.
* '''Inscribed angle''': An angle whose vertex is on the circle, and whose sides each intersect the circle at another point.

=== Areas ===

* '''Disk''': The region enclosed by a circle
* '''Sector''': Region bounded by two radii and the arc delimited by them.
